# Where it lives
The map is **inline SVG inside `index.html`**, in `<div id="mapWrap">`, between two marker comments:

```html
<!-- COLORMAP:BEGIN generated by tools/colorpedia.py build - do not edit by hand -->
<div class="mapPane active" data-map="hex">
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 780.00 784.78" width="780.00" height="784.78" shape-rendering="crispEdges">
<g stroke="#444444" stroke-width="1" stroke-opacity="0.25">
  <polygon points="400.00,28.66 395.00,37.32 385.00,37.32 380.00,28.66 385.00,20.00 395.00,20.00"
           fill="#473f2d" data-hex="#473f2d" data-name="藍媚茶 · Aikobicha"><title>藍媚茶 · Aikobicha #473f2d</title></polygon>
  ...
</g>
</svg>
</div>
<!-- COLORMAP:END -->
```

Since 2026-09-30 the block holds **one pane per saturation plate**, in this order:
`<div class="mapPane active" data-map="vivid" data-label="Vivid">`, then `strong`, `soft`, `muted`
(`data-label` is the tab text). Only the pane with class `active` is visible; the tabs above the map switch it.
Each pane has its own `<svg>` and `viewBox`; CSS scales every plate to the same size, so plates with fewer colors
get bigger cells. `#ffffff` appears once in every pane (the center); every other hex appears in exactly one pane.

`tools/colorpedia.py build` replaces everything between the markers. **Do not edit polygons by hand**:
the next build overwrites them, and hand edits were the main source of errors in the original map
(see [/map/audit-2026-09.md](/map/audit-2026-09.md)).

# One polygon = one color
| Attribute | Required | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | yes | browser | 6 vertices of a regular flat-top hexagon, circumradius 10, two decimals. Vertex order: angles 0°, 60°, … 300° (screen coordinates, so it starts at the right vertex and goes clockwise). |
| `fill` | yes | browser | The color. Must equal `data-hex`. |
| `data-hex` | yes | JavaScript | Lowercase `#rrggbb`. This is the **key** the app uses to find the entry in `colors.json` (`findColor`). A polygon whose `data-hex` is not in `colors.json` is shown but does nothing on hover or click. |
| `data-name` | informative | JavaScript (overwritten) | Names joined with ` · ` (Japanese names as `kanji · romaji`). `hydrateMapTooltips()` rewrites it from `colors.json` at startup, so `colors.json` is the source of truth for names. |
| `<title>` | informative | browser tooltip | `names + " " + hex`, also rewritten at startup. |

The shared thin grey outline sits on the wrapping `<g>`, so it is not repeated per polygon.
Polygons are written in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right), which keeps diffs small.

# Classes the app adds at runtime
* `.dim`: the color is filtered out by the current tab, family or search. Opacity 0.1 and `pointer-events: none`.
* `.sel`: the selected color (white 2px outline). The app also moves the selected polygon to the end of its
  parent, because SVG paints in document order and neighboring cells would otherwise cover half the outline.

# Size of the viewBox
Width and height come from the placed cells plus a 20px margin (see [/map/grid-geometry.md](/map/grid-geometry.md)).
CSS scales the SVG (`.mapWrap svg { max-width:100%; max-height: calc(100vh - 260px) }`), so the numbers
can change whenever colors are added.
